source.quote: The `frontmatter` object MUST be identical in content to the frontmatter of the `SKILL.md` it describes.
The final `<skill-path>` segment of the entry's `uri` MUST equal `frontmatter.name`, per Resource Mapping.
Implementations SHOULD ignore keys under this prefix that they do not recognize.

requirements.exclusion: Ignoring a metadata key leaves nothing on the wire.

source.quote: Within a server's listing, names SHOULD be unique, but they are not guaranteed to be.
Hosts MUST NOT assume name uniqueness.

requirements.exclusion: Binds how the host resolves skill names against other servers and its own filesystem skills: a recording holds one session with one server and none of the host's other origins, and name resolution produces no message.

source.quote: When two entries in one listing collide on `name`, hosts MUST disambiguate them (for example by their distinguishing path segments) rather than silently discarding or preferring one.

requirements.exclusion: Binds how the host resolves skill names against other servers and its own filesystem skills: a recording holds one session with one server and none of the host's other origins, and name resolution produces no message.

source.quote: When skills from different origins collide on `name`, hosts MUST resolve the name within a per-origin namespace, identifying servers by a host-assigned label.

requirements.exclusion: Binds how the host resolves skill names against other servers and its own filesystem skills: a recording holds one session with one server and none of the host's other origins, and name resolution produces no message.

source.quote: An MCP-served skill MUST NOT silently shadow, or be silently substituted for, a same-named skill from any other origin, whether another server or the host's own filesystem skills.

requirements.exclusion: Binds how the host resolves skill names against other servers and its own filesystem skills: a recording holds one session with one server and none of the host's other origins, and name resolution produces no message.

source.quote: `resources` is REQUIRED on every skill entry and takes one of two forms: an array of `SkillResource` objects enumerating the skill's files (`SKILL.md` and every supporting file), or the string `"dynamic"`.
When `resources` is an array, it MUST be complete. It lists every file of the skill, each exactly once, including an entry whose `uri` equals the skill's top-level `uri`.
Each `uri` MUST be the skill's `SKILL.md` or a file within the skill's directory.
Each entry MUST carry `size`, the length in bytes of the file's raw content (the same bytes the `digest` covers).
When a skill's content is generated dynamically, such that stable digests cannot be published, the server MUST set `resources` to the string `"dynamic"` instead of an array.

requirements.exclusion: Its antecedent — content generated so that stable digests cannot be published — is the server's own knowledge. An array of digests and the string `"dynamic"` are both valid forms, and SKILL-034 judges that one of them is present.

source.quote: An entry with no `resources` at all, or with any value other than an array or `"dynamic"`, is invalid, and hosts MUST NOT load it.

requirements.exclusion: Loading is the host placing content in the model's context, which no message marks: a `resources/read` of the skill's `SKILL.md` is transport, not a load (the page says so), so a read after an invalid entry convicts nothing. The server's half — an entry without a valid `resources` — is SKILL-034.

source.quote: Hosts MAY decline to load such skills, and server authors SHOULD expect that some hosts will.

requirements.exclusion: An expectation held by a server's author is not behaviour.

source.quote: Hosts MUST support skills up to and including these limits

requirements.exclusion: The capacity of the host: a recording shows what was served and read, not what the host could have accepted.

source.quote: Servers SHOULD NOT serve a skill that exceeds either limit.
A host that declines a skill on this basis SHOULD tell the user why rather than fail silently on a later read.

requirements.exclusion: Binds what the host shows its user, which strategy rule 2 keeps out: none of it is a message.

source.quote: A server declaring this extension MUST implement the `skills/list` method, which returns entries for the skills it serves.
The `resultType` field MUST be set to `"complete"` on `ListSkillsResult`, as it is the standard result shape for the `skills/list` request.
Hosts MUST NOT treat an empty or partial listing as proof that a server has no skills, and MUST support loading a skill given only its URI

requirements.exclusion: How a host reasons from a listing, and whether it can load a skill by URI alone, are host capabilities; a session in which it never does either is conforming, and one in which it does looks like any `skills/get`.

source.quote: `ListSkillsResult` extends `CacheableResult`, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are REQUIRED, as they are on `tools/list` and `resources/list`, and carry the same semantics.
A server declaring this extension MUST implement the `skills/get` method, which returns the entry for a single skill named by the URI of its `SKILL.md`.
The `resultType` field MUST be set to `"complete"` on `GetSkillResult`, as it is the standard result shape for the `skills/get` request.
`params.uri` MUST be the URI of a skill's `SKILL.md`.
If the URI does not identify a skill the server serves, the server MUST return error `-32602` (Invalid params), the same code `resources/read` uses for unknown resources.
A server MUST answer for every skill it serves, whether or not that skill appears in its `skills/list` result.

requirements.exclusion: What a server serves is its own state at the moment of the call: a skill listed earlier and refused later may have been withdrawn in between, which the page allows (an entry is a point-in-time snapshot), so a refusal convicts nothing.

source.quote: `GetSkillResult` extends `CacheableResult`, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are REQUIRED, as they are on `resources/read`, and carry the same semantics.
